text.en: A comet streaks across the sky with a tail miles long.

The poem describes a comet rampaging through the heavens day and night. It is faster than a cheetah, with a tail miles long, and bigger than a mountain. As it nears the Sun its outer ice melts, forming the bright tail.
The poem links science and poetry: comets are bodies of ice and dust that orbit the Sun. The poet uses comparisons to show their speed and size and creates a sense of wonder about the universe.
The warm-up crossword revises the solar system: Moon, Venus, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, Earth and the Sun. Learn light-year and spectacle.
